Beneath a sky of ashen silk, the ocean stirs—  
A briny expanse where sapphire currents twist,  
Its surface fretted by zephyrs that whisper myths  
Of drowned empires and coral-kissed tombs.  

The tide, a fickle bard, recites in foam,  
Revealing glistening scars along the shore—  
Abalone gleam, a crab’s sidelong chore,  
Then drags the moment back to liquid gloom.  

Far out, where waves convulse with thunderous yawn,  
The deep holds court in indigo repose:  
Leviathans glide through midnight throes,  
While phosphorescent constellations spawn.
